trust_decision.summary: Untrusted: the request `multipart/form-data` body. What is decided, and where: at what cost — and with which multi-value semantics — every form entry is normalised into `context.body` is settled per key inside four `for (const key of form.keys()) { if (body[key]) continue; const value = form.getAll(key); ... }` loops (three in the dynamic handler, one emitted as generated source by the web-standard adapter), before any parse hook or schema validation runs; `form.getAll(key)` rescans the whole entry list for every key, so a body with n distinct keys costs n^2.

landing_point.why: The summary says inefficient formdata normalisation, and the only hand-written multipart parser in the tree is this `case 'multipart/form-data'` block, sitting immediately above `normalizeFormValue` (src/dynamic-handle.ts:126-169) — so both keywords of the report land in this one file. The path that actually serves a default app is not here: with `aot` defaulting to true (src/index.ts:387, 8098-8100) the same normalisation is emitted as a string literal by the adapter, which is invisible to a reader who stays with the handler.

fix_sites.entry_point: HTTP route whose body is declared `multipart/form-data` (or inferred from a t.File/t.Object schema) served by the dynamic handler, i.e. `new Elysia({ aot: false })` + app.handle/app.fetch
HTTP route with `app.onParse('formdata')` / `onParse('multipart/form-data')` registered, dynamic handler
HTTP route with a multipart request and no registered parse hook — the raw content-type fallback switch, dynamic handler

compiled/AOT route (default config; ELYSIA_AOT!=='false') via app.handle/app.fetch/listen, including the Bun adapter (src/adapter/bun/index.ts:214-221 spreads this composeHandler) and the Cloudflare adapter (src/adapter/cloudflare-worker/index.ts:23-24)
fix_sites.module_kind: adapter codegen (handler source emitted as a template string)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: src/adapter/web-standard/index.ts:61-63 — the same entry-normalisation loop, re-written as generated source inside the adapter's formData() code generator (src/adapter/web-standard/index.ts:42-125)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: That copy is not runnable code but text a code generator emits (`fnLiteral` assembled for composed/AOT handlers), so it reads as build/codegen infrastructure rather than a request parser — and the report and its repro lead to the dynamic handler, so the adapter-generated path looks like a separate optimisation concern.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Repeated keys must still aggregate into an array: `tags` appended three times has to arrive as ['tag1','tag2','tag3'], several Files under one key have to arrive as a File[], and a JSON object string next to a File has to be merged into {file}/{files} (src/dynamic-handle.ts:143-168). A fix that takes the changelog wording literally and swaps `form.getAll(key)` for `form.get(key)` silently collapses those to one value; an over-hardening fix that caps entries/keys per body or rejects large forms breaks the same legitimate multi-file and tag-list uploads.

O6_input_shapes: single string value under a key (`name`)
repeated key with several strings → array (tags x3 → ['tag1','tag2','tag3'], test/type-system/formdata.test.ts:724-728)
repeated key with several Files → File[] (src/adapter/web-standard/index.ts:74-84)
JSON object string value (`{...}`) parsed into an object (src/dynamic-handle.ts:127-140)
JSON array string value (`[...]`) parsed into an array
JSON object string + File(s) under the same key merged into {file}/{files} (src/dynamic-handle.ts:152-168)
optional formData (`let form; try{...}catch{}`) — empty or unparsable body (src/adapter/web-standard/index.ts:45-47)
dangerous keys `__proto__` / `constructor` / `prototype` inside nested names (src/adapter/web-standard/index.ts:51-59, src/dynamic-handle.ts:76)

O7_producer.where: src/utils.ts:943-981 — the public `form()` helper (re-exported at src/index.ts:8279) serialises an object into FormData by appending one entry per array element, which is what produces the repeated-key shape, and records parallel metadata under ELYSIA_FORM_DATA that only the client-side type checker reads (src/type-system/index.ts:100-104). The normalisation loops never call it; they only see the platform's decoded entries.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A Bun-specific `parser.formData` override in BunAdapter.composeHandler that builds the body with Bun-native APIs
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The adapter already overrides composeHandler.headers with a Bun-only fast path (`c.request.headers.toJSON()`); adding a faster Bun form parser next to it is the same kind of per-runtime optimisation.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A Cloudflare-specific multipart normalisation emitted from the adapter's composeGeneralHandler override
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This adapter already replaces a piece of the composed handler (error404) to work around a worker-only constraint, so a worker-specific body path would follow the existing pattern.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A fast multipart branch inlined directly into the composed-handler emitter instead of delegating to adapter.parser.formData
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Body parsers are already spliced into the generated source at two separate places keyed on the content type; a maintainer chasing the hot path could inline an unrolled loop at either site and create a fifth copy.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A real multipart decoder inside the universal ElysiaRequest shim (it currently throws for anything that is not already a FormData)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The shim exists to carry non-Web-standard transports; whoever adds a Node/Deno body path there will need to decode entries, and the shortest route is to copy the loop rather than import the handler's normaliser.

O9_family: Algorithmic complexity / denial of service in multipart body normalisation (CWE-407), with a multi-value interpretation conflict on repeated form keys (CWE-436)

O10_build.language: TypeScript (runs on Bun; also Cloudflare Workers and any Web-standard runtime)
O10_build.toolchain: bun (bun test, bun build.ts -> tsup/esbuild), tsc --project tsconfig.test.json for type tests; runtime deps cookie, exact-mirror, fast-decode-uri-component, memoirist, peer @sinclair/typebox; node_modules is not committed at the pinned tree, so `bun install` is needed before anything runs
O10_build.project_tests: bun test over test/: test/type-system/formdata.test.ts (multipart with repeated keys, JSON+file merge, nested ObjectString/ArrayString, zod and typebox validators), test/type-system/files.test.ts and test/validator/body.test.ts (t.File bodies), test/core/formdata.test.ts (the form() encoder), test/core/dynamic.test.ts (aot:false handler behaviour). None of these sends a multipart body through the dynamic handler: the nine test files that mention FormData contain no `aot: false` app, so the three dynamic-handler loops are covered only indirectly.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Take the changelog wording literally — replace `form.getAll(key)` with `form.get(key)` (or keep `getAll` but memoise it) in the one loop the repro reached — which drops repeated-key aggregation for tags and multi-file uploads and leaves the other three loops quadratic.

out_of_scope_notes: The urlencoded parser (src/parse-query.ts) and the response-side `form()` encoder (src/utils.ts:943-981) contain related parsing work but are outside this advisory's multipart normalisation protection, so they were not counted as routes.
Adapters published outside this repository (e.g. @elysiajs/node) were not examined; nothing outside this tree was pursued.
unverified: repo_mb could not be measured (no shell in this session); the tree is ~284 files with the largest source files being src/index.ts (8k+ lines) and the type-system, so `tiny_repo` is plausible but not asserted without a byte count.
The GHSA/CVE text was not available; the protection and its scope were inferred from the one-commit fix diff and the code at the pinned commit.
present_in_latest for O8 is moot — no uncovered route was found at the pinned commit — and no latest tree was available in any case.

Whether a timing-based hidden test can separate the n^2 loop from a linear one reliably depends on the body-size limit the harness allows: the gap is only measurable with a few thousand distinct keys in one multipart body, which is a test-design risk, not a code question.

O7 is recorded against the public `form()` serialiser because it is the only in-repo producer of the repeated-key shape; the entry multiplicity itself is produced by the runtime's FormData decoder behind `request.formData()`, which is outside the tree.

O1 counts the four code sites as four entry points; three of them are branches of one handler selected by route configuration (declared body type, parse hook, raw content type) and the fourth is the default AOT path, so a stricter reading would call it two implementations.
